R420.note: Gate::authorize('delete', $order) before the delete, matching the sibling actions and the existing OrderPolicy::delete; nothing else changed.

R421.note: Magic-byte detection replaces the client-supplied ContentType check, extension now follows detected type, GUID name outside webroot retained; the stricter acceptance and message changes are the fix itself and are stated, and IFormFile's read stream supports the Seek(0) rewind.

R422.note: Secure = true added to CookieOptions; no other change.

R423.note: Same Gate::authorize('delete', $order) fix as the sibling actions, backed by the existing OrderPolicy::delete; nothing else changed.

R424.note: HttpUtility.HtmlEncode on the only untrusted value in an HTML body context; null ticketRef still yields an empty string as before.

R425.note: jku resolver removed and IssuerSigningKeys pinned to a trusted URL closes the vector, but keys are now fetched once in the constructor (key rotation breaks validation until restart, and a fetch failure now throws at construction) - neither stated - and the added ValidAlgorithms=RS256 restriction rejects tokens the issuer may legitimately sign with other RSA/EC algorithms that the original accepted.

R426.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding() with the OrderContext as root keeps property reads and arithmetic while rejecting T(), constructors, beans and method calls, exactly as the contract requires.

R427.note: Generic 'Invalid order ID format' replaces e.getMessage(); status and content type unchanged, and the message change is the fix and is stated.

R428.note: rawComment is entity-encoded at the point of HTML interpolation with the same escaper already used for authorName; the function rename is stated and has no observable effect.

R429.note: Dropping the shell entirely for file()+strpos closes the injection, but file() loads the whole daily access log into memory (grep streamed it), which can exhaust memory_limit on a large log and fail the endpoint - the write-up claims 'identical functionality' and does not mention this; the proc_open argv-array form would have preserved grep's streaming semantics.

R430.note: unserialize(..., ['allowed_classes' => [ShoppingCart::class]]) keeps the wire format and the existing instanceof fallback; legitimate cookies still restore.

R431.note: password_verify() is the right API, but the loose == check only worked if the stored column is plaintext, so after the change every existing login fails until rows are rehashed; the write-up states the hash-at-registration precondition but not that existing stored passwords must be migrated.

R432.note: escape-html applied to the untrusted note (and, stated, to the stored subject/status, which render identically); build confirms the dependency resolves.

R433.note: bcrypt.compare against the stored hash with a valid-format dummy hash for unknown users closes the bypass; the stored field name passwordHash is assumed from a model not shown, and the unknown-user message now reads 'Invalid credentials' as a deliberate anti-enumeration measure the write-up explains.

R434.note: IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync(context) is the correct explicit check for a JSON-bound minimal API endpoint; the new header-token requirement is inherent to the fix and stated, though a failed check surfaces as an unhandled AntiforgeryValidationException (500) rather than a 400.

R435.note: encode_entities($cgi->param('note')) calls param() in list context, so ?note=<payload>&note=q passes 'q' as encode_entities' unsafe-chars argument and the payload is emitted unencoded (confirmed by running encode_entities with a second argument in a scratch directory); the single-value case is fixed, and encoding ticket_id too is harmless and stated.

R436.note: GetRelativePath(...).StartsWith("..") closes the uploads-evil sibling bypass, but GetRelativePath returns the target unchanged when the paths share no root (it does not throw as the write-up claims), so an absolute path on another drive or a UNC path - which the original StartsWith check rejected - now passes the check and is read; StartsWith("..") also rejects legitimate filenames beginning with two dots, and the symlink/cross-drive handling claims are false.
